item.description:
Agent Keyring now stays out of the way and makes credential access easier to understand.
- adds a menu bar app, while keeping normal Dock and app-switcher behaviour when a window is open - rebuilds Access Rules around Ask each time, Allow automatically and Blocked, with clearer bulk changes and AI-assisted review - makes Apple Passwords imports safer, clearer and more useful when something fails - replaces the JSON-first command line with human commands such as `agent-keyring find example.com` and `agent-keyring copy password example.com` - keeps the command and Codex instructions linked to the installed app so they update together

Sharper first-run guidance and a clearer product demo.
- makes the copy-and-paste AI policy assistant a primary workflow - explains automatic, Apple Watch or Touch ID, and blocked access at a glance - installs the Codex integration without requiring a restart - replaces simulated product frames with native macOS window captures

First public preview.
- mirrors supported Apple Passwords credentials into encrypted local storage - lets you ask each time, allow automatically or block each credential - requests Touch ID or Apple Watch approval before releasing protected secrets - includes a Codex skill and CLI that keep secrets out of command output - uses Sparkle for signed updates from GitHub Releases
